title: IdentityServer
description: IdentityServer is an OpenID Connect and OAuth 2.0 framework for ASP.NET Core. It lets you issue access tokens, handle user authentication, and secure APIs.

data.text: IdentityServer implements OpenID Connect and OAuth 2.0 for ASP.NET Core applications. It acts as an identity provider, issuing access tokens and identity tokens so that client apps can authenticate users and call protected APIs.

data.title: Minimal IdentityServer Setup

terms.definition: An identity layer built on OAuth 2.0 that lets apps verify user identity.
A credential used to call a protected API on behalf of a user.
A permission boundary that controls what an access token allows.

data.title: Duende IdentityServer
data.text: IdentityServer is now a commercial product called Duende IdentityServer. A free license is available for development and non-commercial use.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: IdentityServer handles token issuance and user authentication
Clients and scopes are configured in code or via stores
It supports standard protocols: OAuth 2.0 and OpenID Connect
data.takeaway: IdentityServer is the standard choice for full-featured identity in .NET.

data.title: Exercise: Configure a Client
data.description: Add a new client to IdentityServer and request a token.
steps: Add a second client with client credentials flow
Set ClientSecret to a known value
Use Postman or curl to request a token from /connect/token
Decode the token on jwt.io and inspect the claims
data.expectedOutcome: You receive a valid access token that can be used to call a protected API.
